name: Embodied First Exam
tagline: Code agents have passed many exams in the digital world. What is their first exam to enter the physical world?
summary: The first exam for code agents in the physical world. Each question is a frozen simulation scene with a goal written for a person; the answer is a program, marked by replaying it in a fresh simulator. The questions come from many benchmark suites and are sat in two modes: privileged, with the simulator open to the agent, and standard, with only the robot.

suites.name: BEHAVIOR-1K
suites.blurb: Full household activities in house-scale scenes, for a mobile two-armed robot.
suites.description: 100 full-length household activities in house-scale scenes. Agents must combine high-level reasoning, long-horizon navigation, and dexterous bimanual manipulation. Scored by average task success with BDDL partial credit.

preview.title: Setup A Bar For A Cocktail Party

suites.name: RoboLab
suites.blurb: Tabletop tasks that test language grounding, from colours and counts to relations and order.
suites.description: 120 tabletop manipulation tasks for a fixed-base arm, built to test language grounding and goal specification rather than locomotion: colour and size references, counting, spatial relations, sorting, ordered stacking, reorientation. Success is a composable predicate over object state, with partial credit from scored subtasks.

suites.name: RoboCasa
suites.blurb: Everyday kitchen skills for a mobile manipulator in procedurally generated kitchens.
suites.description: Everyday kitchen tasks for a mobile manipulator in large procedurally generated kitchens: opening and closing doors and drawers, turning knobs and faucets, pressing buttons, and picking and placing between counters, cabinets, sinks, stoves and appliances, single- and multi-stage. We keep the 29 tasks with an official demonstration at the pinned commit whose demonstration re-verifies as a reference on a frozen instance (its first episode's initial state). Each task passes or fails on the environment's own success check on the state after the last action, with no partial credit, and runs in two modes: unlimited (privileged: full simulator state, unlimited resets, one replayable trajectory handed in) and limited (standard: the robot's own four cameras, one episode, no reset).
suites.edition: RoboCasa v0.2 @ 756598a, our selection of 29 tasks (exam @ 8c5594a43)

robots.name: Franka Panda on an Omron base

suites.name: RoboCasa365
suites.blurb: Atomic and long composite kitchen activities from RoboCasa's 365-task suite.
suites.description: RoboCasa's 365-task kitchen suite for the same mobile manipulator: atomic skills and long composite activities across cooking, cleaning, storing and serving. We keep 50 of the families with a validated demonstration, chosen by a fixed rule (12 atomic, 38 composite, in SHA-256 order of their names), one frozen instance each. Each task passes or fails on the environment's own success check on the state after the last action, with no partial credit, and runs in two modes: unlimited (privileged: full simulator state, unlimited resets, one replayable trajectory handed in) and limited (standard: the robot's own four cameras, one episode, no reset).

robots.name: Franka Panda on an Omron base

suites.name: RoboCasa-GR1
suites.blurb: A Fourier GR1 humanoid with dexterous hands, picking and placing at a counter.
suites.description: A Fourier GR1 humanoid with two dexterous hands at a kitchen counter: picking objects from one container or surface and placing them in another, including novel objects, and placing into a cabinet, drawer or microwave and closing it. We keep all 24 environments with an official demonstration, one frozen instance each (the demonstration's initial state). Each task passes or fails on the environment's own success check on the state after the last action, with no partial credit, and runs in two modes: unlimited (privileged: full simulator state, unlimited resets, one replayable trajectory handed in) and limited (standard: the humanoid's own six cameras, one episode, no reset).
suites.simulator: robosuite @ 51cc017 (1.5.1, mink whole-body IK) / MuJoCo 3.2.6 (RoboCasa GR1 tabletop)

suites.name: MetaWorld+
suites.blurb: All 50 Meta-World v3 environments for a Sawyer arm, one frozen instance each.
suites.description: All 50 of Meta-World's v3 environments for a Sawyer arm (reward v2), one frozen instance each: push, pick and place, open doors, drawers and windows, press buttons, turn dials and faucets, insert pegs, hammer, sweep and more. Each task passes or fails on Meta-World's own success check on the state after the agent's last action, with no partial credit, and runs in two modes: unlimited (privileged: full simulator state, unlimited resets, one replayable trajectory of at most 500 actions handed in) and limited (standard: a robot behind a service, four fixed cameras and the arm's own state, one episode, no reset). Privileged is reported as a control; the standard mode is the benchmark.
suites.edition: our benchmark (exam @ 8c5594a43): Meta-World v3 @ 59fc34d, all 50 environments

suites.name: VLABench
suites.blurb: Manipulation from language: attributes, common sense and multi-step chores.
suites.description: Language-conditioned manipulation for a Franka Panda at a table: selecting by attribute, common sense, semantic and spatial descriptions, physical question answering by pressing buttons, and multi-step tasks (heating food, setting a table, playing poker). We keep the 36 of VLABench's native tasks whose recorded expert re-verifies on a frozen instance, one instance each. Each task passes or fails on VLABench's own success check (its termination condition), with no partial credit, and runs in two modes: unlimited (privileged: every entity's pose, VLABench's skills as planning primitives, unlimited resets, one replayable trajectory handed in) and limited (standard: four cameras and the arm's own state, one episode, no reset).
suites.edition: VLABench @ cf588fe, our selection of 36 tasks (exam @ 8c5594a43)

suites.name: HumanoidBench
suites.blurb: Whole-body locomotion and manipulation for a Unitree H1 humanoid.
suites.description: Whole-body tasks for a simulated Unitree H1 humanoid, bare or with two Shadow dexterous hands: locomotion (walking, stairs, hurdles, balancing, a maze, sitting) and whole-body manipulation (doors, cabinets, a bookshelf, pushing and lifting, a cube in each hand). Each episode is scored by HumanoidBench's own dense reward, summed over the episode, against its own success bar. We keep the 9 hardest of its 32 registered tasks plus one fixture, and run each in two modes: unlimited (full simulator state, unlimited resets, one replayable trajectory handed in) and limited (a robot behind a service: cameras, joint readings and an IMU, one episode without resets).
suites.edition: cb11890 (upstream), our selection of 9 tasks and a fixture (2026-10-04; 24 until then)

suites.name: MolmoSpaces
suites.blurb: Zero-shot episodes in unseen houses, for a Franka FR3 and an RB-Y1 mobile robot.
suites.description: Ai2's zero-shot evaluation episodes for robot policies in unseen houses: a Franka FR3 picks, places (into a receptacle, next to an object, by colour), opens and closes fixtures, and a Rainbow RB-Y1 mobile manipulator navigates to an object and opens a room door. We keep one upstream episode per family, 8 in all: of three candidates a fixed rule picks per family (cluttered targets, upstream's Hard configurations, far and unseen navigation targets, three different houses), the hardest and most representative in GPT-6 Luna's runs. Each task passes or fails on upstream's own `judge_success()` at the end of the episode, with no partial credit, and runs in two modes: unlimited (privileged: the simulator's full state, upstream's kinematics, unlimited resets, one replayable trajectory handed in) and limited (standard: the robot's own cameras with depth and its proprioception, one episode, no reset).
suites.edition: molmo-spaces 0.2.9, benchmark molmospaces-bench-v2/20260415; our selection of 8 episodes (exam @ e46be110c,

suites.name: KinDER
suites.blurb: Physical reasoning for planning and control: throw, balance, sweep, scoop, pack.
suites.description: Physical reasoning for robot planning and control, kept apart from perception and language: a simulated TidyBot++ mobile manipulator throws, balances, sweeps, scoops, stacks into cupboards, sorts, clears and packs. Each episode passes or fails on KinDER's own goal check (an object's centre inside a goal region, and the like), with no partial credit. We keep 5 of its 31 task families (the 4 hardest, scored, and one fixture), one variant each, and run each in two modes: unlimited (full simulator state and the goal check, unlimited resets, one replayable trajectory handed in) and limited (a robot behind a service: its base and wrist cameras, odometry and joint readings; one episode without resets).
suites.edition: 5b2dbac (upstream), our selection of 4 tasks and a fixture (2026-10-04; 11 until then)
suites.simulator: MuJoCo 3.3 (KinDER's Dynamic3D environments); PyBullet for two kinematic tasks now excluded

suites.name: RoboPaint
suites.blurb: A robot arm with a brush paints the picture it is shown, stroke by stroke, from calligraphy to oils.
suites.description: 82 brush targets for a Franka Panda with a brush: Chinese calligraphy in kaishu (35) and xingshu (16), lettering (10), acrylic (10) and oil (11), each in both modes. The target has to be written or painted with strokes, the way a person does, not coloured in: writing fails when a long brush path is made of thin marks, and a painting has a path budget and its strokes must be sweeps, not zigzag, serpentine or contour-offset fills. Success needs the picture to match and the process rules to hold; work within the rules keeps a continuous score.
suites.simulator: ManiSkill 3.0.1 / SAPIEN 3.0.3 + brush models (calligraphy, broad nib, libmypaint 1.6.1)

suites.name: RoboTwin 2.0
suites.blurb: Fifty bimanual tabletop tasks for a dual-arm ALOHA-AgileX.
suites.description: Fifty bimanual tabletop manipulation tasks on a dual-arm ALOHA-AgileX (four other embodiments supported), each defined as one Python class: a scene builder, a success predicate and a scripted expert that RoboTwin uses to generate its public 100k-episode dataset. Domain randomisation (clutter, textures, lighting, table height) is a switch we leave off. Success is the task's own `check_success()` at the end of the episode, all-or-nothing.
suites.edition: ICML 2026 paper (arXiv 2506.18088); code `main` @ 6dde571 (2026-09-14); assets HF revision 981c92a

suites.name: MuJoCo Playground (manipulation)
suites.blurb: Manipulation environments of MuJoCo Playground, for ALOHA 2 and a Franka Panda.
suites.description: The ten manipulation environments of Google DeepMind's MuJoCo Playground: ALOHA 2 bimanual hand-over and peg insertion, Franka Panda pick-and-place, cabinet opening and pushing, and in-hand cube rotation with the LEAP and Aero hands. Playground is an RL training suite: each env defines a dense reward, not a success test. We run its scene XMLs in plain MuJoCo with our own success tests; four envs are built so far.
suites.simulator: MuJoCo 3.3.7 (plain MuJoCo on the CPU; upstream trains in MJX / MuJoCo Warp)

suites.name: DexToolBench
suites.blurb: Dexterous tool use with a hammer, a marker, an eraser, a brush, a spatula or a screwdriver.
suites.description: Twenty-four dexterous tool-use tasks from SimToolReal: 6 tool categories (hammer, marker, eraser, brush, spatula, screwdriver) x 2 real objects x 2 motions. Each task is a start pose and a sequence of goal poses for the tool, extracted from a human RGB-D demo; the score is task progress, the fraction of goals reached in order. Upstream runs it in Isaac Sim / Isaac Gym; we run SimToolReal's own MuJoCo sim2sim scene, rebuilt, with each category's table props.
suites.simulator: MuJoCo 3.3.7 (our port; upstream runs Isaac Sim / Isaac Gym)

suites.name: RoboWits
suites.blurb: Tabletop tasks that need a physical insight, like a ruler to align things or a funnel to pour.
suites.description: 30 seed tabletop tasks for a fixed bimanual robot, each requiring a physical insight rather than a longer motion: use a ruler to align, a dustpan to sweep, a funnel to pour, an inclined plane to move a box. 163 published mutations vary the scene while keeping the parent task's success predicate. Scored by the task's own success check.

suites.name: ManiGuard
suites.blurb: Manipulation safety. A task counts only if no safety rule was broken on the way.
suites.description: A manipulation safety benchmark from the NU IDEAS Lab: tabletop tasks for a Franka Panda with long fin-ray fingers, each with a safety specification in linear temporal logic over physics predicates (dropped, upright, on top of, closed, touching), checked after every control step. A task counts only if the goal holds and no rule was ever broken.

suites.name: robosuite example
suites.blurb: The reference task every contributor starts from: stack one cube on another.
suites.description: The exam's example task: a Franka Panda stacks a cube in robosuite. It shows the task layout every suite follows and is offered in privileged mode only.

incoming.name: HazardArena

notes.title: Solved means marked 1
notes.text: The verifier marked the answer 1 on a fresh replay.

notes.title: Two modes, never mixed
notes.text: Privileged is the open-book mode, standard the closed-book one; they are scored apart. Standard attempts that allowed resets are not counted.

notes.title: Head to head
notes.text: Only the questions every ranked model sat count. GPT-6 Luna sat all of them; the others sat its misses plus a sample.

notes.title: Ranked from {min_suites} suites
notes.text: A model is ranked once it has marked answers in {min_suites} suites. Smaller runs are listed under the board.

notes.title: The same budget
notes.text: One attempt per question and mode, under the same limits for every model.

recognition.lead: Every task names its author, and every suite credits its upstream benchmark. A proposal for the maintainers:

credits.what: A suite accepted into the exam: proposal, tasks, image and evidence
A family of tasks added to a suite already in the exam
A human review of one family (PROTOCOL §2.7)
A verified exploit or task bug, with its fix merged
A full evaluation run of the exam, logs delivered
